title: 4.6 Small Group · Group 1

noticeAndWonder.context: Evelyn is visiting family in Canada. She sees the sign shown on the highway and wonders whether 100 kilometers per hour is faster or slower than 100 miles per hour. How can Evelyn determine which is faster: 100 kilometers per hour or 100 miles per hour?
wonderStarters: I wonder what would happen if…

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Bridge Engineering
revealWordProblem.text: The Golden Gate Bridge's two main cables are each about 7,650 feet long. A supply company sells cable-protection wrap in spools measured in yards. How many yards of protective wrap does one full cable need? Show your work using a conversion factor.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: 1 yard = 3 feet, so converting feet to the larger unit (yards) means dividing by the conversion factor: 7,650 ÷ 3 = 2,550 yards. One cable needs 2,550 yards of protective wrap.

turnAndTalk.question: The cabinet blueprint uses feet but the parts catalog uses inches. Why do you have to convert, and which is the bigger unit, a foot or an inch?
turnAndTalk.kernel: A foot is bigger than an inch, so I must convert to compare or combine the measurements.

stems.en: I have to convert because the blueprint uses ___ but the catalog uses ___.
stems.es: Tengo que convertir porque el plano usa ___ pero el catálogo usa ___.
Un/Una ___ es más grande que un/una ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Students explain a foot is the larger customary unit (12 inches) and that mixed units must be converted to the same unit before working with them.
turnAndTalk.extend: Predict: when you change feet into inches, will the number get bigger or smaller? Explain using the size of each unit.
extendStems: Switching to a smaller unit means ___.

turnAndTalk.question: How did you use a conversion factor like '1 ft = 12 in' to fill in the ratio table, and how did you decide whether to multiply or divide?
turnAndTalk.kernel: I multiply when going to a smaller unit and divide when going to a bigger unit.

stems.en: ___ equals ___ because the conversion factor is ___.
stems.es: ___ es igual a ___ porque el factor de conversión es ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Students use the conversion factor as a ratio, multiply going to smaller units (5 ft x 12 = 60 in) and divide going to larger units (48 in / 12 = 4 ft).
turnAndTalk.extend: Feet-to-inches uses multiply but inches-to-feet uses divide, even though both use '12.' Explain why the same conversion factor leads to opposite operations.
extendStems: I multiply when ___ but divide when ___.
The same factor works both ways because ___.

turnAndTalk.question: A doorway is 80 inches tall and a new cabinet is listed as 7 feet. Your friend says it won't fit because 7 feet is 82 inches. Will it fit, and where is the error?
turnAndTalk.kernel: 7 feet is 84 inches, which is taller than the 80-inch doorway, so it will not fit.

stems.en: Since ___ inches is ___ than 80 inches, the cabinet ___ fit.
stems.es: Como ___ pulgadas es ___ que 80 pulgadas, el gabinete ___ caber.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Students convert 7 ft to 84 in (not 82), compare 84 > 80, and conclude the cabinet will not fit; they catch the friend's arithmetic error.
turnAndTalk.extend: How many inches would you need to trim off the cabinet to make it fit, and is that even possible for a real cabinet? Justify your reasoning.
extendStems: You would need to remove ___ inches because ___.
That is or is not realistic because ___.

turnAndTalk.question: During practice on Convert Measurement Units, what strategy did you use when a problem felt tricky?
turnAndTalk.kernel: Multiply when changing to a smaller unit, and divide when changing to a bigger unit.

stems.en: I knew my answer was reasonable because ___.
stems.es: Supe que mi respuesta era razonable porque ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Listen for students naming a specific strategy tied to 6.AT.3c — not just "I multiplied." They should connect steps to the key idea.
turnAndTalk.extend: How would you help a classmate who made the common mistake from today's lesson? Use one vocabulary word.
extendStems: I would tell them to ___ first because ___.
The mistake happens when you ___ instead of ___.

launch.narrative: This is your support small group for Lesson 4.6. We're going to slow this down and build it together, one step at a time. You can ask a question any time — that's what this group is for.
launch.contextImage: Arcade cabinet blueprint with measurements in mixed units — feet, inches, and yards

How many inches are in 1 foot? How many feet in 1 yard?
wonderPrompts: How do you decide whether to multiply or divide when converting?

conceptIntro.heading: Let's build it together — How do I change one measurement unit into another?
conceptIntro.intro: A unit is a standard amount used to measure, like a foot or an inch. A conversion factor is a ratio that relates two units, like 1 foot = 12 inches. We'll walk through a worked example, try one together, then you'll try a few with hints right there when you need them.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Multiply when changing to a smaller unit, and divide when changing to a bigger unit.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: The cabinet is 5 feet tall. I want to know how many inches that is.
My conversion factor is 1 foot = 12 inches.
Inches are smaller than feet, so I multiply: 5 × 12 = 60.

weDo.title: Let's try together
lines: A wire is 4 yards long. The factor is 1 yard = 3 feet.
Feet are smaller than yards, so do we multiply or divide? (Multiply)
Now a metric example: a power cable is 3 meters long. The factor is 1 meter = 100 centimeters.
Centimeters are smaller than meters, so we multiply: 3 × 100 = 300 centimeters.
Sentence frame — say it with me: "The multiples/steps I need are ___ , and the answer is ___ ."

youDo.title: Now you try — with support
lines: Try the practice problems below. The hint button is right there whenever you get stuck — use it, that's smart.
Remember the key idea: Multiply when changing to a smaller unit, and divide when changing to a bigger unit..

explore.instructions: Quick warm-up together: Use conversion factors to complete the ratio table. Convert each measurement to the target unit.

discourse.prompt: How do you decide whether to multiply or divide when converting units?
discourse.sentenceFrame: When converting from a ___ unit to a ___ unit, I ___ by the conversion factor because ___.

approaching.stem: How many inches are in 7 feet?
choiceFeedback: There are 12 inches in every foot.
hints: The key fact: 1 foot = 12 inches. You have 7 feet and want inches.
Going from a BIGGER unit (feet) to a SMALLER unit (inches) means you multiply.
Set up 7 × 12 — seven groups of 12 inches.

approaching.stem: How many feet are in 3 yards?
choiceFeedback: There are 3 feet in every yard.
hints: The key fact: 1 yard = 3 feet. You have 3 yards and want feet.
Big unit (yards) to small unit (feet) means multiply by the conversion factor 3.
Set up 3 × 3 — three yards, each worth 3 feet.

approaching.stem: How many ounces are in 4 pounds?
choiceFeedback: There are 16 ounces in every pound.
hints: The key fact: 1 pound = 16 ounces. You have 4 pounds and want ounces.
Pounds are bigger than ounces, so converting to ounces means multiplying by 16.
Set up 4 × 16. (Break it up: 4 × 10 = 40 and 4 × 6 = 24, then add.)

choiceFeedback: There are 12 inches in one foot.
hints: This one goes the OTHER direction: inches (small) to feet (big), so the number of units gets smaller.
Small unit to big unit means divide. Ask: how many groups of 12 inches fit in 24 inches?
Set up 24 ÷ 12.

approaching.title: approaching — Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Convert 2 yards of rope to feet

approaching.correctWork: Feet are smaller than yards, so you multiply (not divide): 2 × 3 = 6 feet. Changing to a smaller unit always gives a bigger number, not a tiny decimal.
hints: You are going from a bigger unit (yards) to a smaller unit (feet). Should the number get bigger or smaller?
Changing to a smaller unit means more of them, so multiply: 2 × 3 = 6 feet.

onLevel.stem: A shelf is 30 inches long. How many feet and inches is that?
choiceFeedback: Divide by 12 and look for a remainder: 30 ÷ 12 = 2 R6.
Find how many complete feet fit, then how many inches left over.
hints: 30 inches is more than 2 feet (24 in) but less than 3 feet (36 in) — so the answer is 2 feet plus some leftover inches.
Divide by 12 to find whole feet; the REMAINDER stays as inches.
Compute 30 ÷ 12: it goes in 2 whole times using up 24 inches. Subtract 30 − 24 to find the leftover inches.

onLevel.title: onLevel — Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Convert 80 ounces of bolts to pounds

onLevel.correctWork: Ounces are smaller than pounds, so you divide (not multiply): 80 ÷ 16 = 5 pounds. Changing to a bigger unit gives a smaller number.
hints: You are going from a smaller unit (ounces) to a larger unit (pounds). Should the number get bigger or smaller?
Changing to a larger unit means fewer of them, so divide: 80 ÷ 16 = 5 pounds.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Convert Measurement Units is applying the conversion factor in the wrong direction — for example, converting 4 feet to inches by dividing (4 ÷ 12 = 0.33 inches) instead of multiplying (4 × 12 = 48 inches), or converting 80 ounces to pounds by multiplying (80 × 16 = 1,280 pounds) instead of dividing (80 ÷ 16 = 5 pounds). Before you answer, ask: am I changing to a SMALLER unit (there will be MORE of them, so multiply) or a BIGGER unit (there will be FEWER of them, so divide)?

exitTicket.stem: Quick check — you've got this: Which is the correct conversion of 5 yards to inches?
exitTicket.explanation: 5 yards × 3 = 15 feet. 15 feet × 12 = 180 inches. Or: 5 × 36 = 180 inches.
choiceFeedback: Convert 5 yards to feet, then feet to inches.
Start with: 5 yards = ? feet. Then convert to inches.
Remember: 1 yard = 3 feet, and 1 foot = 12 inches.
hints: Yards to inches is a TWO-step trip: yards → feet → inches (or use 1 yard = 36 inches in one jump).
Multiply twice: yards × 3 gives feet, then feet × 12 gives inches. Or multiply yards × 36 directly.
Step 1: 5 × 3 = 15 feet. Step 2: multiply that 15 by 12 to land on inches.

smallGroup.label: Extra Support
smallGroup.who: Pull 3–5 students who struggled on the formative check / exit ticket for this lesson.
moves: Open with the worked example (I Do) — think aloud, don't just show.
Do the We Do together; require every student to say the sentence frame.
Release to the practice problems; the hint ladder is the safety net.

Watch for the common mistake: A common mistake in Convert Measurement Units is applying the conversion factor in the wrong direction — for example, converting 4 feet to inches by dividing (4 ÷ 12 = 0.33 inches) instead of multiplying (4 × 12 = 48 inches), or converting 80 ounces to pounds by multiplying (80 × 16 = 1,280 pounds) instead of dividing (80 ÷ 16 = 5 pounds). Before you answer, ask: am I changing to a SMALLER unit (there will be MORE of them, so multiply) or a BIGGER unit (there will be FEWER of them, so divide)?.
Close with the exit-ticket check — celebrate the growth.
